content.value_statement: Inconsistent UI components slow product work and create visual drift. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use shared tokens, layouts, and component patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use design tokens instead of hard-coded values.
Maps spacing, color, and typography token names to documented uses.
Provides TSX examples for Box, HStack, VStack, Text, Button, Input, and Card.
Shows screen, form, and list item layout patterns.
Identifies anti-patterns such as raw platform components and inline styles.
limitations: Does not include source code for the component library.
Assumes the project already defines the documented token names.
Focuses on TSX and React Native style examples.
Does not validate accessibility, performance, or visual output.

use_cases.title: Create Product Screens
use_cases.description: Assemble screens with Screen, Box, Stack, Text, Button, Input, and Card patterns.

use_cases.title: Review UI Consistency
use_cases.description: Check whether components use shared tokens instead of inline styles, raw values, or platform primitives.

use_cases.title: Document Component Usage
use_cases.description: Turn component examples and token rules into clear guidance for a team wiki or pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Use Core Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI and replace raw platform components with documented core components where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component to use spacing, color, and typography tokens from the core component guidelines.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Form Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a form layout plan using VStack, Input, Button, validation states, and loading states from the core component patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this reusable component API for token-based props, variant handling, and anti-patterns against the core component skill.

output_examples.input: A product screen uses raw View and Text elements with inline padding, color, and font sizes.
output_examples.output: Recommended update: replace raw layout elements with Box and VStack, map spacing to token values, and use Text color and size tokens. Keep the existing content and behavior unchanged.

output_examples.input: A card component accepts numeric padding and free-form variant strings.
output_examples.output: Review result: restrict padding to approved token values, document supported variants, and pass visual differences through the Box component.

output_examples.input: A list item layout mixes custom containers, hard-coded borders, and manual icon color values.
output_examples.output: Suggested pattern: use HStack for the row, VStack for text, semantic border tokens, and a tertiary color token for the icon.

best_practices: Start with core layout components before adding custom containers.
Use semantic color and typography tokens for every visible text state.
Document new variants with the same token names and component props used in the skill.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding spacing, color, or font values when a token exists.
Importing raw platform View or Text components for standard UI.
Adding inline styles that bypass shared component props.

faq.question: Does this skill install a component library?
faq.answer: No. It provides usage guidance for a project that already has core components.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include real source files?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains guidance and TSX examples in SKILL.md only.

faq.question: Can it help with React Native screens?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use React Native style component names and TSX patterns.

faq.question: Does it define every token value?
faq.answer: No. It lists common spacing, color, and typography tokens that the project should already support.

faq.question: Can it review existing UI code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare code against the documented token and component patterns.
